proposal.diagnosis: All 49 missed transfers and denied transfer boardings in the baseline run were concentrated entirely on Muni Bus lines (specifically on Muni 6 with 30 denied transfers, Muni 5 with 14, and Muni 57 with 5). Under local_only context policy and without transfer optimization tools or hold rules, connecting buses departed just minutes before incoming transfer passengers could board (e.g., denied transfer boardings occurred after only 4-6 minutes of wait time). Zero service holds occurred, leaving connecting riders stranded and driving up overall passenger delay.
proposal.rationale: To protect connection windows without excessive schedule disruption, we introduce a declarative transfer hold rule targeting Muni Bus, scoped to trigger when at least 2 incoming transfer riders are detected, bounding the maximum vehicle hold to 3 minutes. In accordance with harness requirements, incoming_transfer_riders signals require shared context (updating context_policy from local_only to transfer_neighbors), and the hold_for_transfer action requires enabling the transfer_optimizer tool. The existing controller hold_load_fraction (0.05) preserves passenger throughput by preventing holds when vehicles are already heavily loaded.
proposal.expected_improvement: Hypothesized reduction in Muni Bus missed transfers from 49 toward fewer than 15, lowering transfer wait times and unserved passenger counts while adding minimal delay to already-boarded passengers due to the 3-minute hold cap and hold load threshold.

proposal.diagnosis: Muni Bus experienced 636 denied boardings and 1,652 unserved passengers, driven by persistent station queues on core routes (such as 57:1 with 155 denied boardings and 15-minute wait times, and 19:1 with 56 denied boardings). Under the baseline policy, dispatch_threshold_local is set to 1.2, requiring queues to exceed 120% of standard vehicle capacity before triggering standby service. Consequently, only 5 standby dispatches occurred (costing 450 out of the 12,000 available supplemental budget) despite 12 available Muni Bus standby vehicle/driver pairs sitting idle while queues hovered between 40 and 65 riders.
proposal.rationale: Rather than introducing multi-operator transfer holds (which failed in v2 by delaying already-boarded passengers for marginal transfer gains), the harness should address the primary failure mode: local capacity shortages on Muni Bus lines. Lowering dispatch_threshold_local from 1.2 to 0.7 enables the local_dispatch_optimizer to deploy standby vehicles earlier when local passenger queues reach 70% of route capacity, absorbing queue spikes on lines 57, 19, 15, and 6 before repeated boarding denials accumulate.
proposal.expected_improvement: Lowering dispatch_threshold_local to 0.7 is hypothesized to increase standby dispatches within the 12-vehicle Muni Bus fleet and 12,000 cost budget, substantially reducing denied boardings from 636 and decreasing unserved passengers and total passenger delay minutes.

proposal.diagnosis: In v3, lowering dispatch_threshold_local from 1.2 to 0.7 was successfully promoted (+3.25% improvement across 4 of 5 seeds), confirming that local standby dispatch responsiveness is the primary lever for clearing urban transit bottlenecks. However, telemetry still shows 1,569 unserved passengers, 427 denied boardings on Muni Bus, and peak queues exceeding 110 riders on lines 57, 6, and 22. At the 0.7 local threshold, routes with queues between 25 and 40 riders (e.g., Muni 30, 28R, M, 12, 19, 29) are denied standby support until queues compound, resulting in cascading boardings denied at minutes 120-162. Additional operating cost is only 3,420 out of the 12,000 budget, indicating ample fiscal and standby vehicle capacity to intervene earlier.
proposal.rationale: By reducing dispatch_threshold_local from 0.7 to 0.45, local agents will trigger supplemental standby dispatches when queue ratios exceed 0.45 rather than waiting for 0.7. This allows Muni Bus agents to dispatch standby vehicles to high-density edges with 25-40 waiting passengers before queues cause denied boardings. This isolates a single parameter hypothesis while preserving all other policies, agent memberships, and toolchains.
proposal.expected_improvement: Standby buses will deploy proactively for edges with moderate-to-high queues, reducing denied boardings across Muni Bus lines, lowering average passenger wait time and total passenger delay without exceeding the 12,000 gross supplemental service budget.
